candidate_relations.reason: Disseminated intravascular coagulation is a systemic coagulopathy not required to explain device-free ear necrosis after prone ventilation.
Calciphylaxis is a calcific arteriolopathy of renal failure, not this histology of bland full-thickness pressure necrosis.
Biopsy showed necrosis with sparse inflammation, not a primary vasculitis.
Purpura fulminans is retiform purpura from acute thrombotic vasculopathy, not pressure necrosis of the helical rim/earlobe.
Sepsis/bacteremia is present but does not explain bilateral ear pressure necrosis after proning.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: S. haemolyticus bacteremia as a comorbid infection

candidate_relations.reason: Necrotizing fasciitis is a rapidly spreading deep soft-tissue infection, not isolated ear-helix pressure necrosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Necrotizing fasciitis versus localized ear necrosis

candidate_relations.reason: Coumadin/warfarin necrosis is not supported; the history is factor VII deficiency and prone positioning, not warfarin.
Ecthyma gangrenosum is typically Pseudomonas septic embolic necrosis, not bland pressure necrosis of the ears.
Warfarin-induced skin necrosis is a different thrombotic dermal necrosis and is not described.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Warfarin-induced skin necrosis versus pressure necrosis

candidate_relations.reason: Septic emboli would be vasculocentric infective infarcts, not pressure-pattern helical/earlobe necrosis after proning.
Staphylococcal scalded-skin syndrome is superficial intraepidermal cleavage, not full-thickness epidermal and adnexal necrosis.

case_quality_flags: Prone positioning with ear necrosis and full-thickness adnexal necrosis without devices fits pressure necrosis; bacteremia is comorbid.
